name: Cement
tile_text: Crusher and mill wear parts and heat-resistant castings for the preheater, kiln and clinker cooler.
desc: Wear and heat-resistant castings for every stage of a cement plant: crushing, grinding, preheater, kiln and clinker cooler.
lede: Castings for every stage of the line, from the limestone crusher to the clinker cooler, each specified for the wear, impact and heat it will meet.
intro: A cement line asks two opposite things of its castings. At the front, parts must survive impact and abrasion at ambient temperature. From the preheater onwards, they must hold their shape and resist scaling in hot, dusty gas. We pour both families and specify each part for the stage it works in.

steps.label: Crushing
steps.name: Crushing
steps.text: Limestone, shale and additives are broken down before grinding. These parts take repeated heavy impact, so toughness comes first and hardness second.

steps.label: Grinding
steps.name: Raw and cement grinding
steps.text: Vertical roller mills and ball mills grind raw meal, coal and cement. Wear here is mostly sliding abrasion, so the harder white irons earn their place, with tough steels where the load is carried.

steps.label: Preheater
steps.name: Preheater
steps.text: Raw meal meets hot kiln gas in the cyclone tower. Castings must keep their shape and resist oxidation and sulphur attack in the lower, hottest stages.

steps.label: Kiln
steps.name: Kiln ends
steps.text: At the kiln inlet and outlet, castings protect the shell and hold the refractory. A failure here stops the whole plant, so we design for life between planned shutdowns.

steps.label: Cooler
steps.name: Clinker cooler
steps.text: Grate plates and bars carry and move red-hot clinker under constant abrasion. The right alloy for each zone and a design that resists warping decide how long a grate lasts.

why: Both families, one foundry
Wear-resistant and heat-resistant alloys poured, treated and tested in the same plant.
Grade set by duty
We ask where the part runs and what it meets before we recommend a grade.
Ready for the shutdown
More than 10,000 patterns on file. Parts machined and fit-checked before dispatch.

name: Mining
tile_text: Feeder, crusher and mill wear parts for moving ore from the pit to the plant.
desc: Crusher liners, mill liners and material-handling wear parts for mines, cast in manganese steel, Cr-Mo steel and white irons.
lede: Wear parts for the feeders, crushers, mills and machines that move ore from the pit to the plant.
intro: In a mine, a liner that fails early costs more in lost tonnes than the part itself. Primary crushers need tough steel that hardens under impact; mills need a balance of toughness and wear; feeders and tracked machines need parts that take both. We cast for each duty and machine where the fit matters.

steps.label: Feeding
steps.name: Feeding and scalping
steps.text: Apron feeders take the full drop of run-of-mine rock. Grizzlies scalp the fines before the crusher. Parts take impact from falling ore and wear from sliding.

steps.label: Primary crushing
steps.name: Primary crushing
steps.text: Jaw and gyratory crushers take run-of-mine rock in heavy, repeated blows. Manganese steel is the standard here because its surface hardens as it is struck.

steps.label: Secondary crushing
steps.name: Secondary and tertiary crushing
steps.text: Cone crushers reduce ore to mill feed. Liner profile and alloy decide the throughput and how often the crusher stops for a change.

steps.label: Grinding
steps.name: Grinding
steps.text: Ball mills grind ore under combined impact and abrasion. Liners must lift the charge without breaking. The trunnions carry it all.

steps.label: Machines
steps.name: Tracked and mobile machines
steps.text: Shovels, mobile crushers and tracked plant run on cast shoes, wheels and rollers that take impact and abrasion while carrying the machine.

why: Heavy pieces in one pour
Single castings up to 7 tonnes, with up to 10 tonnes of liquid metal in one pour.
Toughness you can check
Chemistry and hardness reported for every heat, traceable to the casting.
Machined to fit
Seats, bores and faces machined to drawing and checked with gauges.

name: Aggregate
tile_text: Jaw plates, cone liners, blow bars and hammers for quarries.
desc: Crusher wear parts for quarries and aggregate producers: jaw plates, cone liners, blow bars, impact plates and hammers.
lede: Crusher wear parts for quarries, where cost per tonne crushed is the number that matters.
intro: Quarries crush everything from soft limestone to abrasive granite. The same crusher needs a different liner for each, so we ask about the rock before we recommend the alloy and the profile.

steps.label: Feeding
steps.name: Feeding and scalping
steps.text: Grizzlies and chutes take the first impact of blasted rock and send the fines around the primary crusher.

steps.label: Jaw crushers
steps.name: Jaw crushers
steps.text: The primary crusher takes the largest rock. Jaw plates must stay tough while their teeth wear evenly.

steps.label: Cone crushers
steps.name: Cone crushers
steps.text: Secondary and tertiary cones shape the final product. Liner life and profile decide both cost and product size.

steps.label: Impact crushers
steps.name: Impact crushers
steps.text: Horizontal-shaft impactors throw rock against the aprons at speed. Blow bars need hardness for wear and enough toughness to survive tramp metal.

why: Alloy matched to the rock
Limestone and granite need different liners, so we ask before we quote.
Patterns on file
More than 10,000 patterns, so many common crusher parts are ready to mould.
Shipped anywhere
Packed and documented for export to plants anywhere in the world.

name: Thermal power and steel
tile_text: Coal crusher and coal mill parts for power stations and wear parts for steel plant material handling.
desc: Coal crusher and coal mill wear parts for thermal power stations and wear parts for material handling in steel plants.
lede: Coal crusher and mill parts for power stations and wear parts for the material-handling lines of steel plants.
intro: A coal-fired station wears out its crushers and its mills; a steel plant wears out the crushers, chutes and spouts that handle its raw materials. Both need abrasion resistance where material slides and toughness where it strikes, specified part by part.

steps.label: Coal handling
steps.name: Coal handling
steps.text: Hammer crushers size coal before the mills. Chutes guide it between conveyors. Parts take impact and abrasion from coal, shale and stone.

steps.label: Coal grinding
steps.name: Coal grinding
steps.text: Vertical bowl and roller mills and tube mills grind coal to fine powder for the boiler. Sliding abrasion dominates, so white irons last longest.

steps.label: Steel plants
steps.name: Steel plant material handling
steps.text: Ore, coke and flux are crushed, conveyed and fed through chutes and spouts that wear by impact and sliding, sometimes while hot.

why_title: Why power and steel plants choose us
why: Wear and heat in one plant
Abrasion-resistant irons, tough steels and heat-resistant steels under one roof.
Tested before it ships
Chemistry and hardness reported for every heat, with NDT where specified.
Ready for outages
Patterns kept on file and parts machined in-house to meet planned shutdowns.

name: Equipment makers
tile_text: Castings machined to drawing for crusher, mill and kiln manufacturers.
desc: Castings and machined components to drawing for crusher, mill, kiln and process equipment manufacturers.
lede: Castings and machined components made to your drawing, for the equipment you build and service.
intro: Original equipment makers need a foundry that works to their drawing, their standard and their schedule. We review the drawing, design the method, cast, heat treat and machine, then send the reports your quality team needs.

steps.label: Drawing review
steps.name: Drawing review and method
steps.text: Our engineers review the drawing for castability, then agree the method, the grade and the inspection plan with you before a pattern is made.
items: Hot spots, shrinkage risks and machining allowances raised before tooling.
Gating and feeding designed in-house, with casting simulation through a specialist partner.
What is tested, how and to which standard, agreed before production.

steps.label: First article
steps.name: Pattern and first article
steps.text: Patterns are made in-house. The first casting is fully inspected and reported before series production starts.
items: Wood, polystyrene and aluminium patterns, cut on a CNC router.
Dimensions, chemistry, hardness and NDT, reported to you.
Series production starts on your sign-off.

steps.label: Series production
steps.name: Series production and machining
steps.text: Castings are poured, heat treated and machined to drawing, each one traceable to its heat.

why: Your drawing, your standard
IS, ASTM, EN or your own specification, with an agreed inspection plan.
From 3 kg to 7 tonnes
Small series and heavy single pieces from the same foundry.
Cast and machined
One supplier for the casting and the machined part.
